Rules:
- All measurements in METERS. Use the plan's dimensions; without dimensions, estimate from the scale or from the bay measurements below.
- Origin at the top-left corner of the building, as the plan appears: x grows to the right, y downward. building.length = size in x; building.width = size in y.
- rows: each row of bays placed side by side. x, y = top-left corner of the row rectangle. direction "horizontal" (the row runs along x: length in x, depth in y) or "vertical" (length in y, depth in x).
- corridor_side = which side the corridor from which products are picked is on: "above" or "below" for horizontal rows, "left" or "right" for vertical ones. Two rows back to back are TWO rows, each with its own corridor side.
- aisle = the aisle code (list below). bays = "odd" (odd bays), "even" (even bays), "all" (all bays of the aisle) or the list of bay codes in that row, e.g. ["01", "03", "05"]. Usually odd bays are on one side of the corridor and even bays on the other.
- numbering_from = "start" if the bay numbers grow with x (horizontal) or with y (vertical); "end" if they grow the other way.
- obstacles: pillars, internal walls, offices, ramps, docks, areas without bays (rectangles: x, y of the top-left corner, length in x, width in y).
- reference: the point where picking starts and returns to (dispatch, dock, checking table).
- Use only the aisles in the list. If the plan does not show the aisle codes, use "aisle": "?" and list the rows in reading order (top to bottom, left to right): the software asks the user to choose the aisle of each one. Do not invent codes.
- If the plan has no bays, return "rows": [] with the building, the obstacles and the reference.
